# Data sources and attribution

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_bench.py from the DATASETS declared in authoring/bench/*.py. Edit those, not this file. -->

Decision Bench bench-v3 has 359 rows. 323 are real records sampled from the public datasets below; the other 36 are written examples (skill improvement), MIT licensed with the code.

**License policy.** A dataset is used only if its own license *and* the terms of the text inside it allow anyone to copy, modify and redistribute it, including commercially (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, public domain). Datasets built on non-commercial or publisher-copyrighted text are not used, even when the dataset itself is MIT. Each row keeps its source license; CC BY-SA rows stay CC BY-SA.

Every real row names its dataset, license, URL, record id and original label in its `source` field. `data/sources/manifest.json` pins the sha256 of every upstream file; `python3 scripts/fetch_sources.py` re-downloads and verifies them. The raw downloads are not committed.

If you are a rights holder and want a row removed, open an issue using the *Data removal request* template, or see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) to report it privately.

<a id="deepset-prompt-injections"></a>
## deepset/prompt-injections

- **Homepage:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/deepset/prompt-injections
- **License:** [Apache-2.0](https://huggingface.co/datasets/deepset/prompt-injections/blob/4f61ecb038e9c3fb77e21034b22511b523772cdd/README.md)
- **What a row contains:** Short chat prompts in English and German, some benign and some trying to override an assistant's instructions, published by deepset; the card does not say who wrote them.
- **Terms of that text:** Apache-2.0. The card's license field is apache-2.0 (a second, misplaced cc-by-4.0 entry inside its dataset_info block is also permissive). No upstream source or other terms are documented for the prompts.
- **Answers from:** the dataset's human annotators (label 0 benign, 1 injection)
- **How rows were chosen:** Records are screened by the written rules in this module's docstring (language, length, a broad offensive-vocabulary block list, no e-mail addresses, phone numbers, web addresses or named private individuals), mapped to an answer by keyword rules, then taken in sha256 order of the record id. Mix: 10 injection, 6 benign (at most 1 German each).
- **What we changed:** None to the text: prompts are shown verbatim. Label 1 is mapped to injection only when an override cue is present and no persona cue is; other label-1 rows are skipped.
- **Cite:** deepset, prompt-injections (Hugging Face dataset), 2023.

```bibtex
@misc{deepset2023promptinjections,
  author       = {{deepset}},
  title        = {prompt-injections},
  year         = {2023},
  howpublished = {\url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/deepset/prompt-injections}}
}
```

<a id="in-the-wild-jailbreak-prompts"></a>
## In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts (JailbreakHub)

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/verazuo/jailbreak_llms
- **License:** [MIT](https://github.com/verazuo/jailbreak_llms/blob/main/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** Prompts that users posted on Reddit, Discord and prompt-sharing websites (FlowGPT, AIPRM, JailbreakChat) between December 2022 and December 2023, collected by the paper's authors.
- **Terms of that text:** MIT. User-posted text, released by the collectors under MIT (the Hugging Face card and the GitHub LICENSE both say MIT); no stricter upstream terms are known. The card adds a disclaimer that the repository "is intended for research purposes only. Any misuse is strictly prohibited." The rows used here come from Reddit (r/ChatGPT, r/ChatGPTJailbreak), Discord (ChatGPT Prompt Engineering, LLM Promptwriting) and FlowGPT; each row's original_label names its platform.
- **Answers from:** community tagging on the source site (the collectors' jailbreak flag)
- **How rows were chosen:** Records are screened by the written rules in this module's docstring (language, length, a broad offensive-vocabulary block list, no e-mail addresses, phone numbers, web addresses or named private individuals), mapped to an answer by keyword rules, then taken in sha256 order of the record id. Jailbreak rows need both an unlock cue and a role-play cue; at most 2 DAN prompts; near-duplicates collapse to one. Mix: 10 jailbreak, 4 benign.
- **What we changed:** None to the text: prompts are shown verbatim.
- **Cite:** Shen, Chen, Backes, Shen and Zhang, "Do Anything Now": Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on Large Language Models, ACM CCS 2024.

<a id="llmail-inject-challenge"></a>
## LLMail-Inject

- **Homepage:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/llmail-inject-challenge
- **License:** [MIT](https://github.com/microsoft/llmail-inject-challenge/blob/main/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** Attack emails that participants of Microsoft's LLMail-Inject challenge (2024–2025) wrote to hijack a simulated email assistant, and the benign inbox emails the organisers wrote for the challenge scenarios.
- **Terms of that text:** MIT. Participants accepted official rules granting Microsoft "an irrevocable, royalty-free, worldwide right and license" to use entries "for any non-commercial or commercial purpose, including ... inclusion into a public dataset" (quoted in Abdelnabi et al. 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09956); the dataset is published under MIT. contact@contact.com is the challenge's fictional target address.
- **Answers from:** the challenge's own records (every submission is an attacker's email; the benign emails are the organisers' inbox fixtures)
- **How rows were chosen:** Attacks: 24 small windows of the Phase 1/Phase 2 logs, kept only when the email names the target address, at most one per team, then the first 12 in sha256 order; benign: the scenario inbox emails of at least 400 characters, de-duplicated by subject, first 12 in sha256 order. Both pass the same content and personal-data screen.
- **What we changed:** None to the text: subject and body are shown verbatim.
- **Cite:** Abdelnabi et al., LLMail-Inject: A Dataset from a Realistic Adaptive Prompt Injection Challenge, arXiv:2506.09956, 2025.

<a id="creddata"></a>
## Samsung CredData

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/Samsung/CredData
- **License:** [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/Samsung/CredData/blob/c09c0c52fc6dae4ae5438ae69ba486f9f8059f0d/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** One to five lines of source, config or documentation files from public GitHub repositories, around a line that secret scanners flagged; CredData supplies the labels and line positions.
- **Terms of that text:** Apache-2.0. CredData's labels and metadata are Apache-2.0; its README says "Each file is under the existing project's license". Each excerpt here keeps its repository's license, read from its license file and recorded per row (source.code_license and code_license_file): MIT, Apache-2.0 or BSD-3-Clause for all 24 rows. The repository and the file's base name are shown (CredData hides both behind ids; the repository is kept for attribution and the base name because it is part of the evidence); nothing that locates the file is.
- **Answers from:** CredData's reviewers, who manually checked every scanner hit against written ground rules
- **How rows were chosen:** Labelled lines from the 305 CredData repositories with a permissive GitHub license, in sha256 order, 8 per label, at most one per repository, filtered by the written rules in authoring/bench/pii.py; six real-credential lines were dropped after reading (CRED_EXCLUDED).
- **What we changed:** Every value CredData judged a real credential, and any other credential-shaped string in the shown lines, is replaced with a random fake of the same length and shape (AWS keys with AWS's documented example pair; provider prefixes broken with EXAMPLE). Only the flagged line and up to two lines either side are shown. So that no row leads a reader to a live secret, every row (whatever its label, so the shape never hints at the answer) keeps only the repository URL and license, the CredData metadata file and Id, and the file's base name. The scrubbed excerpts are committed; the commit, directory path and line number of the originals are recorded nowhere in this repository.
- **Cite:** Yun et al., Project CredData: A Dataset of Credentials for Research, Samsung, 2021.

```bibtex
@misc{sr-cred21,
  author       = {JaeKu Yun and ShinHyung Choi and YuJeong Lee and Oleksandra Sokol and WooChul Shim and Arkadiy Melkonyan and Dmytro Kuzmenko},
  title        = {Project {CredData}: A Dataset of Credentials for Research},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/Samsung/CredData}},
  year         = {2021}
}
```

<a id="agentrx"></a>
## AgentRx benchmark

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/microsoft/AgentRx
- **License:** [MIT](https://github.com/microsoft/AgentRx/blob/7a18c79708e7671be15124460f4f7296107c2a55/LICENSE.txt)
- **What a row contains:** Failed agent runs with the failure steps marked: τ-bench retail customer-service chats (a gpt-4o agent with the store's tools, a simulated customer, the store policy and the customer's hidden instructions) and Magentic-One multi-agent runs on AssistantBench web tasks (the same logs as Who&When's Hand-Crafted set), with the text the agents read from web pages and tools.
- **Terms of that text:** MIT. The GitHub repository (the copy used) is MIT ("Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation"). The Hugging Face copy (microsoft/AgentRx) is CC BY 4.0 and asks visitors to share contact details before downloading; it states no other condition, and it was not used (its terms were not accepted). τ-bench (sierra-research/tau-bench) is MIT; its retail customers, orders and products are synthetic. The Magentic-One logs come from Who&When (MIT) and their tasks from AssistantBench (Apache-2.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/AssistantBench/AssistantBench); they quote short snippets of third-party web pages (search results, business listings) that the agents retrieved. The agent turns are gpt-4o outputs.
- **Answers from:** AgentRx's human annotators (three annotators, grounded-theory coding; mean pairwise Cohen's kappa 0.89 reported in the paper)
- **How rows were chosen:** Failure steps whose category maps to an option and whose label passes the re-checks in _tc1 (right speaker, visible evidence, read by hand), in sha256 order, scarcest option first, at most 5 per option, one row per run and per τ-bench customer (two for the scarcest option).
- **What we changed:** Categories are mapped to six options (TC1_CATEGORY). The transcript runs up to one turn after the reviewed step; long turns are cut to a head and a tail with "…[N chars truncated]" marked (the same cap for every turn but the reviewed one), and long Magentic-One runs show the task, the plan and the turns just before the step, with the omitted turns marked. Nothing is rewritten.
- **Cite:** Barke et al., AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories, arXiv:2602.02475, 2026. Runs from τ-bench (Yao et al., 2024) and Who&When (Zhang et al., 2025).

```bibtex

  journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.02475},
  year    = {2026},
  url     = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02475}
}
```

<a id="whoandwhen"></a>
## Who&When

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/mingyin1/Agents_Failure_Attribution
- **License:** [MIT](https://github.com/mingyin1/Agents_Failure_Attribution/blob/b2bae5c5b06d681d04ea5e9b63b7a30525c04925/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** Logs of failed runs of LLM multi-agent teams (CaptainAgent-built AutoGen groups and Magentic-One) on AssistantBench web tasks, with the task, its correct answer and the text the agents read from web pages and tools.
- **Terms of that text:** MIT. The logs are MIT on GitHub; the Hugging Face copy (Kevin355/Who_and_When) states no license. The task and answer come from AssistantBench, whose Hugging Face dataset is apache-2.0 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/AssistantBench/AssistantBench); its GitHub code repository is under the AI Pubs OpenRAIL-S license, which covers its source code, not the task data. Logs quote short snippets of third-party web pages (business listings, search results) that the agents retrieved. GAIA-task logs are not used.
- **Answers from:** Who&When's human annotators
- **How rows were chosen:** AssistantBench logs of at most 40 KB whose labelled agent speaks the labelled step, in sha256 order, one per question, at most 4 rows with the same answer, 24 rows at most.
- **What we changed:** Every turn is cut to the same cap (head and tail kept, "…[N chars truncated]" marked) so the transcript fits 12,000 characters; turns are numbered; nothing is rewritten.
- **Cite:** Zhang et al., Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems, ICML 2025. Tasks from AssistantBench (Yoran et al., 2024).

<a id="swe-agent-trajectories"></a>
## nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories

- **Homepage:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories
- **License:** [CC-BY-4.0](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories/blob/68195a1450865274106246d0d0296a1d6807b88e/README.md)
- **What a row contains:** Runs of a SWE-agent coding agent (driven by fine-tuned open-weight models) on real GitHub issues from SWE-bench-extra and SWE-bench: the issue text, the agent's actions, what the environment returned (often repository code) and the final patch.
- **Terms of that text:** CC-BY-4.0. The card: "licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license. However, please respect the license of each specific repository on which a particular instance is based." Each row's repository license was read and is recorded as code_license (all MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause or BSD-3-Clause). Issue text was posted by GitHub users. The card also says users of the model outputs "must comply with the Llama 3.1 License" (https://www.llama.com/llama3_1/license/); that license's conditions apply to using the agents' outputs to train or improve a model.
- **Answers from:** the repository's own tests (not a human): the dataset's target field
- **How rows were chosen:** Submitted runs with a patch of at most 5,000 characters from 64 evenly spaced 2-row windows of the dataset, in sha256 order, 12 per outcome, every row from a different repository.
- **What we changed:** Only the issue, the last 6 actions with their observations and the final patch are shown; long text keeps a head and tail with "…[N chars truncated]" marked. The hidden tests' logs are never shown.
- **Cite:** Golubev et al., Leveraging training and search for better software engineering agents, Nebius blog, 2024 (Hugging Face dataset nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories).

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/tree/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard

<a id="cfpb-complaints"></a>
## CFPB Consumer Complaint Database

- **Homepage:** https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/
- **License:** [CC0-1.0](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BEE-spoke-data/consumer-finance-complaints/blob/088cc7308d4afc2a880f2329d08e2f7a09188ec6/README.md)
- **What a row contains:** Complaint narratives that US consumers wrote to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and agreed to have published, with the product they chose when filing; read from a February 2024 Hugging Face mirror (BEE-spoke-data/consumer-finance-complaints) of the CFPB database.
- **Terms of that text:** Public domain. The mirror is marked CC0-1.0. The CFPB says "Information created by the CFPB is in the public domain" (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/website-privacy-policy/); the narratives are written by consumers, published only with their consent and scrubbed of personal information by the CFPB (shown as XXXX). On 14 August 2026 the CFPB stopped publishing narratives and said it "considers previously published narratives to be in the public domain for Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) purposes" (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/about-us/newsroom/the-cfpb-to-cease-discretionary-publication-of-complaint-narratives-and-visualizations/). No license or restriction from the consumers themselves is known.
- **Answers from:** the consumer's own product choice when filing
- **How rows were chosen:** Narratives of 250–1,800 characters from 16 fixed 100-row pages of the mirror, in sha256 order of the complaint id, 4 per product team, minus the complaints in TR3_SKIP.
- **What we changed:** None to the narrative (surrounding whitespace stripped); only the date received is kept from the other fields.
- **Cite:** Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Consumer Complaint Database; narratives are published with the consumer's consent and scrubbed of personal information by the CFPB (shown as XXXX). Read through the CC0 Hugging Face mirror BEE-spoke-data/consumer-finance-complaints.

```bibtex
  note         = {Narratives read from the Hugging Face mirror BEE-spoke-data/consumer-finance-complaints (February 2024)}
}
```

<a id="hagrid"></a>
## HAGRID

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/project-miracl/hagrid
- **License:** [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/project-miracl/hagrid/blob/7ffab03942e93d3138b0dbd14ad0a844f8a075d5/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** A question written by MIRACL's annotators, the English Wikipedia paragraphs they marked relevant to it, and an answer GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) wrote from those paragraphs, citing them by number.
- **Terms of that text:** CC-BY-SA-3.0. The paragraphs are English Wikipedia text (MIRACL's 1 February 2019 dump), licensed by Wikipedia's contributors under CC BY-SA 3.0 and the GFDL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Copyrights); each row links the Wikipedia articles its paragraphs come from and carries CC BY-SA 3.0. The questions (MIRACL) and HAGRID's answers and labels are Apache-2.0.
- **Answers from:** HAGRID's four trained annotators, who judged whether each answer sentence is fully supported by the passages it cites
- **How rows were chosen:** English dev answers judged for attributability, filtered by the written rules in authoring/bench/eval_judging.py (consistent and informative answers, every sentence cited, no self-contradicting labels, no sensitive topics) and a review that left out answers a reviewer could label either way (listed with reasons), then balanced across labels and answer types in a fixed hash order; one answer per question.
- **What we changed:** None: the question, every passage and the answer are shown in full, as the model received and wrote them.
- **Cite:** Kamalloo et al., HAGRID: A Human-LLM Collaborative Dataset for Generative Information-Seeking with Attribution, arXiv:2307.16883, 2023.

```bibtex
  journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.16883},
  year    = {2023}
}
```

<a id="begin"></a>
## BEGIN (Wizard of Wikipedia part)

- **Homepage:** https://github.com/google/BEGIN-dataset
- **License:** [CC-BY-4.0](https://github.com/google/BEGIN-dataset/blob/6e65f0d5a1ed1b9574643a7640ff1678d4e979b5/wow/LICENSE)
- **What a row contains:** A crowdworker's chat message and one Wikipedia sentence from the Wizard of Wikipedia dataset, and the reply a fine-tuned dialogue model (T5, GPT-2, DoHA or CTRL-dialog) generated from them.
- **Terms of that text:** CC-BY-SA-3.0. The knowledge sentence is Wikipedia text (CC BY-SA 3.0, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Copyrights); the chat messages are Wizard of Wikipedia (Facebook, CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/facebookresearch/ParlAI/blob/main/parlai/tasks/wizard_of_wikipedia/LICENSE_DOCUMENTATION); BEGIN's replies and labels are CC BY 4.0 (see begin/NOTICE). Rows carry CC BY-SA 3.0.
- **Answers from:** the majority vote of three trained BEGIN annotators
- **How rows were chosen:** Fully and not fully attributable replies of at least eight words whose word overlap with the knowledge is between 40% and 85%, without sensitive topics and without replies a review found mislabelled (listed with reasons), balanced across labels and the four models in a fixed hash order; one reply per knowledge sentence.
- **What we changed:** None: the message, knowledge sentence and reply are shown verbatim, including the models' tokenised spacing.
- **Cite:** Dziri et al., Evaluating Attribution in Dialogue Systems: The BEGIN Benchmark, TACL 2022.

## MT-Bench human judgments

- **Homepage:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments
- **License:** [CC-BY-4.0](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments/blob/f7d2896d2cc5d80f8b55c2bbc722613555233c25/README.md)
- **What a row contains:** One of the 80 MT-Bench questions written by LMSYS, and the first-turn responses of two of six models (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude-v1, Vicuna-13B, Alpaca-13B, LLaMA-13B).
- **Terms of that text:** CC-BY-4.0. Questions and responses are part of the CC BY 4.0 dataset; the questions are also released in FastChat under Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/blob/587d5cfa1609a43d192cedb8441cac3c17db105d/LICENSE).
- **Answers from:** MT-Bench's expert judges (mostly graduate students with expertise in the question's topic), unanimous across at least two judges
- **How rows were chosen:** Turn-1 pairs judged by at least two experts who all preferred the same response (no ties), excluding coding questions, a question asking the model to be a real living person, LLaMA-13B (a base model) and pairs a review found arguable either way (listed with reasons); four pairs from each of seven categories in a fixed hash order.
- **What we changed:** Only the first turn is shown. The two responses are shown in a fixed order that puts the preferred one first on every other row; each row records the order.
- **Cite:** Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks.

<a id="contractnli"></a>
## ContractNLI

- **Homepage:** https://stanfordnlp.github.io/contract-nli/
- **License:** [CC-BY-4.0](https://stanfordnlp.github.io/contract-nli/resources/contract-nli.zip)
- **What a row contains:** Full texts of real non-disclosure agreements: exhibits filed with the US SEC (EDGAR) and NDA templates or forms that companies, universities and public bodies posted on the web, collected by the ContractNLI authors (Hitachi America).
- **Terms of that text:** CC-BY-4.0. The dataset zip holds LICENSE (CC BY 4.0) and TERMS (saved as data/sources/contractnli/LICENSE and LICENSE-TERMS). Hitachi America's TERMS grant use "in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License" and give a notice address for anyone who believes the dataset "incorporates any of your work". The SEC says "Information presented on sec.gov is considered public information and may be copied or further distributed by users of the web site without the SEC's permission" (https://www.sec.gov/privacy). The web templates carry no license of their own; agreements with a copyright notice are not used (COPYRIGHT_NOTICE), and each row links the agreement's original URL (document_url). Some agreements name business contacts in their notice clauses; their phone numbers and e-mail addresses are removed.
- **Answers from:** ContractNLI's annotators, who also marked the evidence spans
- **How rows were chosen:** Test-split agreements of at most 10,000 characters, 10 pairs per label in sha256 order of (document, hypothesis), one row per agreement, at most 2 per hypothesis, minus the pairs excluded by the rules above.
- **What we changed:** The hypothesis and the full agreement text are shown as ContractNLI has them, except that e-mail addresses and phone/fax numbers are replaced with placeholders; the labels are renamed (Entailment -> yes, Contradiction -> says_opposite, NotMentioned -> not_addressed).
- **Cite:** Koreeda and Manning, ContractNLI: A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts, Findings of EMNLP 2021.

```bibtex
}
```
